summary: Allocates and populates two parallel vertex-buffer offset arrays (start and end offsets) hanging off an output descriptor, one entry per animation/render element. Reserves the array storage up front via a vtable allocation call sized by element count, then loops the element descriptors, deriving each element's byte span from its width, a stride field and a divisor, allocating per-element sub-buffer space and recording start/end offsets. Called by MediaBufferAlloc.

operations.description: Load the output descriptor (this+0x180) into v1 and the divisor (this+0x114) into v2.
Call the allocation function through the vtable at this+0x4 with (this, 1, 8 * element count), reserving the offset-array storage.
Seed loop counter to 0, store the allocated base at out+0x38 and the end pointer (base + 4 * element count) at out+0x3C of the output descriptor.
Only iterate when the element count at this+0x20 is greater than 0; otherwise return the count unchanged.
Walk the element descriptor array at this+0xC4 starting at descriptor+0xC, advancing 21 dwords (84 bytes) per element.
Per element compute span v6 = width * stride / this+0x114 * (divisor + 4) and v9 = width * stride / this+0x114, where width is at descriptor+0xC and stride at descriptor+0x24.
Call the allocation function through the vtable at this+0x4 again with (this, 1, 8 * span) and add 4 * v9 to obtain this element's buffer start offset.
Write the element start offset into the out+0x38 array at index counter, and the element end offset (start + 4 * span) into the out+0x3C array at the same index; increment the counter.
Advance the element pointer by 21 dwords; the loop terminates once the counter reaches the element count at this+0x20.
Return the final element counter value.

unresolved: Meaning of the this+0x114 divisor and of the width/stride element fields is inferred only from arithmetic shape; exact units unknown.
The allocation-call semantics (what 8 * size and the second argument 1 select) depend on the vtable implementation at this+0x4.
The (divisor + 4) factor in the span computation is a raw product of the decompiled expression, not a confirmed layout constant.
